goal.sl: Razumeš in uporabljaš glagole s tremi besedami (put up with, look forward to, come up with) in tiste, ki pomenijo več kot njihovi deli (come across, take after, turn down).
goal.de: Du verstehst und verwendest Verben aus drei Wörtern (put up with, look forward to, come up with) und solche, die mehr bedeuten als ihre Teile (come across, take after, turn down).
goal.it: Capisci e usi i verbi di tre parole (put up with, look forward to, come up with) e quelli che vogliono dire più delle loro parti (come across, take after, turn down).
goal.en: You can understand and use three-word verbs (put up with, look forward to, come up with) and those that mean more than their parts (come across, take after, turn down).

say.sl: **I can't put up with this noise.** (Tega hrupa ne prenesem.) Nekateri glagoli imajo dve mali besedi: **put up with** (prenašati), **run out of** (ostati brez), **get on with** (razumeti se z). Vse tri ostanejo skupaj, zaimek na koncu: **I can't put up with it.** Spreminja se le glagol: **We've run out of coal.** Američani rečejo tudi **get along with**.
say.de: **I can't put up with this noise.** (Diesen Lärm ertrage ich nicht.) Manche Verben haben zwei kleine Wörter: **put up with** (ertragen), **run out of** (keins mehr haben), **get on with** (gut auskommen mit). Alle drei bleiben zusammen, das Pronomen am Ende: **I can't put up with it.** Nur das Verb ändert sich: **We've run out of coal.** In Amerika auch **get along with**.
say.it: **I can't put up with this noise.** (Non sopporto questo rumore.) Alcuni verbi hanno due parole piccole: **put up with** (sopportare), **run out of** (restare senza), **get on with** (andare d'accordo con). Tutte e tre restano unite, il pronome alla fine: **I can't put up with it.** Cambia solo il verbo: **We've run out of coal.** In America anche **get along with**.
say.en: **I can't put up with this noise.** Some verbs have two small words: **put up with**, **run out of**, **get on with**. All three stay together, the pronoun last: **I can't put up with it.** Only the verb changes: **We've run out of coal.** Americans also say **get along with**.

say.sl: **I'm looking forward to the fair.** (Veselim se sejma.) **look forward to** (veseliti se): tu je **to** mala beseda, za njim samostalnik ali -ing: **I look forward to seeing you.** **come up with** (domisliti se): **Sam came up with a plan.** **keep up with** (dohajati): **I can't keep up with Jack on the fell.**
say.de: **I'm looking forward to the fair.** (Ich freue mich auf den Markt.) **look forward to** (sich freuen auf): Hier ist **to** ein kleines Wort, danach ein Nomen oder -ing: **I look forward to seeing you.** **come up with** (sich ausdenken): **Sam came up with a plan.** **keep up with** (mithalten mit): **I can't keep up with Jack on the fell.**
say.it: **I'm looking forward to the fair.** (Non vedo l'ora che arrivi la fiera.) **look forward to** (non vedere l'ora di): qui **to** è una parola piccola, dopo c'è un nome o -ing: **I look forward to seeing you.** **come up with** (farsi venire in mente): **Sam came up with a plan.** **keep up with** (stare al passo con): **I can't keep up with Jack on the fell.**
say.en: **I'm looking forward to the fair.** **look forward to**: here **to** is a small word, with a noun or -ing after it: **I look forward to seeing you.** **come up with** is to think of: **Sam came up with a plan.** **keep up with** is to go as fast: **I can't keep up with Jack on the fell.**

say.sl: **Mrs Birkett is cutting down on coal.** (Gospa Birkett porabi manj premoga.) Še nekaj: **cut down on** (zmanjšati), **look up to** (občudovati), **look down on** (gledati zviška), **get away with** (ostati nekaznovan), **make up for** (nadoknaditi) in britanski **fall out with** (spreti se): **Harry broke the window and got away with it.** **Edna fell out with Maggie.**
say.de: **Mrs Birkett is cutting down on coal.** (Mrs Birkett verbraucht weniger Kohle.) Noch ein paar: **cut down on** (weniger verbrauchen), **look up to** (aufschauen zu), **look down on** (herabschauen auf), **get away with** (ungestraft davonkommen), **make up for** (wettmachen) und britisch **fall out with** (sich zerstreiten): **Harry broke the window and got away with it.** **Edna fell out with Maggie.**
say.it: **Mrs Birkett is cutting down on coal.** (La signora Birkett consuma meno carbone.) Altri ancora: **cut down on** (ridurre), **look up to** (ammirare), **look down on** (guardare dall'alto in basso), **get away with** (farla franca), **make up for** (compensare) e il britannico **fall out with** (litigare con): **Harry broke the window and got away with it.** **Edna fell out with Maggie.**
say.en: **Mrs Birkett is cutting down on coal.** A few more: **cut down on** is to use less, **look up to** to admire, **look down on** to think less of, **get away with** not to be punished, **make up for** to make good, and British **fall out with** to quarrel: **Harry broke the window and got away with it.** **Edna fell out with Maggie.**

say.sl: **I came across an old letter in the attic.** (Na podstrešju sem {m:naletel|f:naletela} na staro pismo.) Dve besedi, svoj pomen, ostaneta skupaj: **come across** (naleteti na), **take after** (biti podoben), **get over** (preboleti), **look into** (raziskati), **run into** (srečati), **go through** (pregledati). Zaimek na koncu: **I came across it.** **Poppy takes after her.**
say.de: **I came across an old letter in the attic.** (Auf dem Dachboden habe ich einen alten Brief gefunden.) Zwei Wörter, eine eigene Bedeutung, sie bleiben zusammen: **come across** (zufällig finden), **take after** (nach jemandem geraten), **get over** (überwinden), **look into** (prüfen), **run into** (zufällig treffen), **go through** (durchgehen). Pronomen am Ende: **I came across it.** **Poppy takes after her.**
say.it: **I came across an old letter in the attic.** (In soffitta mi sono imbattut{m:o|f:a} in una vecchia lettera.) Due parole, un significato tutto loro, restano unite: **come across** (imbattersi in), **take after** (assomigliare a), **get over** (riprendersi da), **look into** (esaminare), **run into** (incontrare per caso), **go through** (controllare). Il pronome alla fine: **I came across it.** **Poppy takes after her.**
say.en: **I came across an old letter in the attic.** Two words, a meaning of their own, and they stay together: **come across** is to find by chance, **take after** to be like a parent, **get over** to get well after, **look into** to find out about, **run into** to meet by chance, **go through** to check. The pronoun last: **I came across it.** **Poppy takes after her.**

say.sl: **They called off the fair.** (Sejem so odpovedali.) Drugi se razdelijo: **turn down** (zavrniti), **bring up** (vzgojiti), **work out** (ugotoviti), **call off** (odpovedati), britanski **sort out** (urediti), **make up** (izmisliti si). Samostalnik stoji na obeh mestih: **They called the fair off.** Zaimek v sredini: **They called it off.** **She turned it down.**
say.de: **They called off the fair.** (Sie haben den Markt abgesagt.) Andere werden getrennt: **turn down** (ablehnen), **bring up** (großziehen), **work out** (herausfinden), **call off** (absagen), britisch **sort out** (in Ordnung bringen), **make up** (erfinden). Ein Nomen steht an beiden Stellen: **They called the fair off.** Ein Pronomen in der Mitte: **They called it off.** **She turned it down.**
say.it: **They called off the fair.** (Hanno annullato la fiera.) Altri si dividono: **turn down** (rifiutare), **bring up** (crescere un figlio), **work out** (capire), **call off** (annullare), il britannico **sort out** (sistemare), **make up** (inventare). Un nome sta in tutti e due i posti: **They called the fair off.** Un pronome in mezzo: **They called it off.** **She turned it down.**
say.en: **They called off the fair.** Others can part: **turn down** is to say no to, **bring up** to raise a child, **work out** to find the answer, **call off** to cancel, British **sort out** to put right, **make up** to invent. A noun stands in both places: **They called the fair off.** A pronoun in the middle: **They called it off.** **She turned it down.**

say.sl: **The milk has gone off.** (Mleko se je pokvarilo.) Isti glagol ima več pomenov, pove ti stavek: **go off** (pokvariti se), **turn up** (pojaviti se), **pick up** (naučiti se sproti), **put up** (prenočiti koga), **work out** (dobro se izteči). **Jack turned up at ten.** **I picked up some English at the inn.** **Mrs Birkett put us up for the night.**
say.de: **The milk has gone off.** (Die Milch ist schlecht geworden.) Ein Verb hat mehrere Bedeutungen, der Satz sagt dir welche: **go off** (schlecht werden), **turn up** (auftauchen), **pick up** (nebenbei lernen), **put up** (bei sich unterbringen), **work out** (gut ausgehen). **Jack turned up at ten.** **I picked up some English at the inn.** **Mrs Birkett put us up for the night.**
say.it: **The milk has gone off.** (Il latte è andato a male.) Un verbo ha più significati, te lo dice la frase: **go off** (andare a male), **turn up** (farsi vedere), **pick up** (imparare strada facendo), **put up** (ospitare), **work out** (andare bene). **Jack turned up at ten.** **I picked up some English at the inn.** **Mrs Birkett put us up for the night.**
say.en: **The milk has gone off.** One verb has several meanings, and the sentence tells you which: **go off** is to go bad, **turn up** to arrive, **pick up** to learn as you go, **put up** to give someone a bed, **work out** to end well. **Jack turned up at ten.** **I picked up some English at the inn.** **Mrs Birkett put us up for the night.**

title.en: A bad week at the inn

exercises.text: On Monday we ran ___ of coal. “I can't put up ___ this cold,” said Mrs Birkett. Then Sam came up ___ a plan: he would bring some from Keswick. While we waited, I came ___ an old letter in the attic. It was from Mrs Birkett's grandmother, and Harry says his mum takes ___ her. On Friday they called ___ the dance because of the snow. Now we're all looking forward ___ the summer.

translation.sl: V ponedeljek nam je zmanjkalo premoga. »Tega mraza ne prenesem,« je rekla gospa Birkett. Potem se je Sam domislil načrta: prinesel ga bo nekaj iz Keswicka. Medtem ko smo čakali, sem na podstrešju {m:naletel|f:naletela} na staro pismo. Bilo je od babice gospe Birkett, in Harry pravi, da je njegova mama podobna njej. V petek so zaradi snega odpovedali ples. Zdaj se vsi veselimo poletja.
translation.de: Am Montag ist uns die Kohle ausgegangen. „Diese Kälte ertrage ich nicht“, sagte Mrs Birkett. Dann dachte sich Sam einen Plan aus: Er würde welche aus Keswick holen. Während wir warteten, fand ich auf dem Dachboden einen alten Brief. Er war von Mrs Birketts Großmutter, und Harry sagt, seine Mutter gerät nach ihr. Am Freitag wurde der Tanz wegen des Schnees abgesagt. Jetzt freuen wir uns alle auf den Sommer.
translation.it: Lunedì siamo rimasti senza carbone. «Non sopporto questo freddo», ha detto la signora Birkett. Poi a Sam è venuto in mente un piano: ne avrebbe portato un po' da Keswick. Mentre aspettavamo, in soffitta mi sono imbattut{m:o|f:a} in una vecchia lettera. Era della nonna della signora Birkett, e Harry dice che sua madre le assomiglia. Venerdì hanno annullato il ballo per la neve. Ora non vediamo tutti l'ora che arrivi l'estate.
translation.en: On Monday we ran out of coal. “I can't put up with this cold,” said Mrs Birkett. Then Sam came up with a plan: he would bring some from Keswick. While we waited, I came across an old letter in the attic. It was from Mrs Birkett's grandmother, and Harry says his mum takes after her. On Friday they called off the dance because of the snow. Now we're all looking forward to the summer.

exercises.text: Mr Dixon ___ the job at the mill (said no to). Mr and Mrs Tyson ___ three children on the farm (raised). Last week Jack ___ Sam in Keswick (met by chance). It took Edna a week to ___ her cold (get well after). In the end we ___ the problem (found the answer to).

translation.sl: Gospod Dixon je zavrnil službo v mlinu. Gospod in gospa Tyson sta na kmetiji vzgojila tri otroke. Prejšnji teden je Jack v Keswicku srečal Sama. Edna je potrebovala teden, da je prebolela prehlad. Na koncu smo rešili težavo.
translation.de: Mr Dixon lehnte die Stelle in der Mühle ab. Mr und Mrs Tyson zogen auf dem Hof drei Kinder groß. Letzte Woche traf Jack in Keswick zufällig Sam. Edna brauchte eine Woche, bis sie ihre Erkältung überstanden hatte. Am Ende fanden wir die Lösung für das Problem.
translation.it: Il signor Dixon ha rifiutato il lavoro al mulino. Il signor Tyson e sua moglie hanno cresciuto tre figli alla fattoria. La settimana scorsa Jack ha incontrato per caso Sam a Keswick. A Edna ci è voluta una settimana per riprendersi dal raffreddore. Alla fine abbiamo risolto il problema.
translation.en: Mr Dixon turned down the job at the mill. Mr and Mrs Tyson brought up three children on the farm. Last week Jack ran into Sam in Keswick. It took Edna a week to get over her cold. In the end we worked out the problem.
